source.note: 英文逐字稿取自 YouTube 字幕；中文為學習用翻譯。版權屬原作者，僅供個人學習。

lines.en: Hello. This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English. I'm Neil.
lines.zh: 哈囉。這裡是 BBC Learning English 的《6 Minute English》。我是 Neil。

lines.en: And I'm Georgie.
lines.zh: 我是 Georgie。

lines.en: Neil, I'm going to play you two sound recordings, and I want you to tell me how you feel when you hear them.
lines.zh: Neil，我要播兩段錄音給你聽，我想請你告訴我，聽到時有什麼感覺。

lines.en: OK.
lines.zh: 好。

lines.en: First this...
lines.zh: 先聽這個……

lines.en: And now this.
lines.zh: 再聽這個。

lines.en: Oh, well, that first clip made me feel really relaxed.
lines.zh: 喔，第一段讓我覺得很放鬆。

lines.en: But the second one – oh, it's horrible!
lines.zh: 但第二段——喔，好可怕！

lines.en: I felt quite stressed out actually.
lines.zh: 其實我覺得壓力好大。

lines.en: Oh no! Well, this little experiment shows how much we are affected by the noise around us.
lines.zh: 喔不！嗯，這個小實驗顯示我們有多容易受到周遭噪音的影響。

lines.en: And that's a problem if you're one of the four billion people around the world who live in cities.
lines.zh: 如果你是全世界 40 億住在城市裡的人之一，這就是個問題。

lines.en: Yes, whether it's the rattle of train tracks, honking car horns, or the roar of aeroplanes overhead, modern cities are full of noise and this can have serious effects.
lines.zh: 對，不管是火車鐵軌的轟隆聲、汽車的喇叭聲，還是頭頂飛機的呼嘯聲，現代城市充滿了噪音，而這可能帶來嚴重的影響。

lines.en: The World Health Organisation reports that by 2050, around 2.5 billion people will experience hearing loss, and exposure to loud noise has been linked to stress and anxiety.
lines.zh: 世界衛生組織報告指出，到 2050 年，大約 25 億人會出現聽力損失，而長期暴露在巨大噪音中也和壓力、焦慮有關。

lines.en: In this episode, we'll be hearing about ways to make our cities quieter, more relaxing places, using some useful new words and phrases.
lines.zh: 在這一集，我們會用一些實用的新單字和片語，聊聊讓城市更安靜、更讓人放鬆的方法。

lines.en: And remember, you'll find all the vocabulary along with a quiz and worksheet on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
lines.zh: 別忘了，所有詞彙以及測驗和學習單，都在我們的網站 bbclearningenglish.com。

lines.en: But now I have a question for you, Georgie.
lines.zh: 不過現在，Georgie，我有個問題要問你。

lines.en: Sound is measured in units called decibels.
lines.zh: 聲音的計量單位叫做分貝。

lines.en: But how many decibels would it be if I whispered?
lines.zh: 那如果我說悄悄話，會是幾分貝？

lines.en: A whisper is speaking like this.
lines.zh: 悄悄話就是這樣說話。

lines.en: Is it: a) 3 decibels, b) 13 decibels, or c) 30 decibels?
lines.zh: 是：a) 3 分貝、b) 13 分貝，還是 c) 30 分貝？

lines.en: Oh, that's really hard.
lines.zh: 喔，這真的好難。

lines.en: I'll go for b) 13 decibels.
lines.zh: 我選 b) 13 分貝。

lines.en: Well, we'll find out the answer at the end of the programme.
lines.zh: 我們會在節目最後揭曉答案。

lines.en: Let's start in one of the noisiest cities in the world – Mumbai in India, where daytime noise levels regularly hit 80 decibels, which is over 20 decibels higher than World Health Organisation recommendations.
lines.zh: 我們先從全世界最吵的城市之一開始——印度的孟買，那裡白天的噪音經常達到 80 分貝，比世界衛生組織的建議值高出 20 分貝以上。

lines.en: Listen to Mumbai native Chhavi Sachdev share her experiences of living in this noisy city with BBC World Service programme People Fixing the World.
lines.zh: 來聽孟買本地人 Chhavi Sachdev 在 BBC 世界廣播節目《People Fixing the World》中分享住在這個吵鬧城市的經驗。

lines.en: I mean, India in general is just really loud.
lines.zh: 我是說，印度整體來說就是非常吵。

lines.en: We are a loud people.
lines.zh: 我們是一個很大聲的民族。

lines.en: We dress loud, we talk loud, we celebrate loud, we watch movies loud.
lines.zh: 我們穿得很大膽（loud）、說話很大聲、慶祝很熱鬧、看電影也開很大聲。

lines.en: When people ask me what I miss about living abroad, I tell them it's the quiet, because after 12 years of living in the US and Europe, when I got back, I realised I couldn't handle it anymore.
lines.zh: 大家問我懷念住在國外的什麼時，我說是安靜，因為在美國和歐洲住了 12 年，回來之後，我發現自己再也受不了了。

lines.en: I'd gotten used to lower levels of noise.
lines.zh: 我已經習慣比較低的噪音了。

lines.en: Chhavi says, Indians talk loud, celebrate loud and dress loud.
lines.zh: Chhavi 說，印度人說話大聲、慶祝熱鬧，穿著也 loud。

lines.en: To dress loud means to wear clothes with bright colours and large, bold patterns.
lines.zh: To dress loud 的意思是穿顏色鮮豔、圖案大又醒目的衣服。

lines.en: When Chhavi returned to India after living overseas, she says she couldn't handle the noise.
lines.zh: Chhavi 在國外住過之後回到印度，她說她受不了那些噪音。

lines.en: If you can't handle something, you find it difficult to deal or cope with.
lines.zh: 如果你 can't handle 某件事，就是你覺得很難處理或應付它。

lines.en: So, what can be done to tackle noise in cities like Mumbai?
lines.zh: 那麼，要怎麼處理孟買這類城市的噪音呢？

lines.en: One interesting approach involves using sound itself to make things feel quieter.
lines.zh: 有一個有趣的方法，是利用聲音本身讓環境感覺更安靜。

lines.en: Soundscaping is the idea of adding certain sounds to busy public spaces so that they sound and feel more relaxing.
lines.zh: Soundscaping（聲景營造）的概念是在繁忙的公共空間加入某些聲音，讓那裡聽起來、感覺起來更放鬆。

lines.en: Sound artist Charles Montambault lives near the Parc des Madelinots, a busy city park in Montreal, Canada.
lines.zh: 聲音藝術家 Charles Montambault 住在加拿大蒙特婁一座繁忙的城市公園 Parc des Madelinots 附近。

lines.en: Charles was inspired to recreate the ocean sounds he heard on holiday in the Magdalen Islands in his city park back home.
lines.zh: Charles 受到啟發，想在家鄉的城市公園重現他在馬德蓮群島度假時聽到的海洋聲音。

lines.en: On BBC World Service programme People Fixing the World, he tells reporter Natasha Fernandes that these sounds included ocean waves and some unusual-sounding sand.
lines.zh: 在 BBC 世界廣播節目《People Fixing the World》中，他告訴記者 Natasha Fernandes，這些聲音包括海浪聲，以及某種聲音很特別的沙子。

lines.en: The sand on the Magdalen Islands can sing.
lines.zh: 馬德蓮群島的沙子會唱歌。

lines.en: When you walk into the sand firmly, the sand makes some squeaky sounds, so that's one sound that is kind of funny, kind of special.
lines.zh: 當你用力踩進沙子裡，沙子會發出吱吱的聲音，所以那是一種有點好笑、有點特別的聲音。

lines.en: Inside the small park, surrounded by busy roads, Charles and his team set up an immersive sound installation in the form of speakers planted in flower beds.
lines.zh: 在這座被繁忙道路包圍的小公園裡，Charles 和他的團隊設置了一個沉浸式的聲音裝置，把喇叭種在花圃裡。

lines.en: So, the installation was really to make this park a little quieter by adding some quiet noises.
lines.zh: 所以這個裝置其實是透過加入一些安靜的聲音，讓這座公園變得安靜一點。

lines.en: So, it's counterintuitive, but you can make a park less noisy by adding some calmer sounds.
lines.zh: 所以這很違反直覺，但你可以透過加入一些比較平靜的聲音，讓公園變得不那麼吵。

lines.en: The sand on the Magdalen Islands is squeaky – it makes a high-pitched sound called a squeak when stepped on.
lines.zh: 馬德蓮群島的沙子是 squeaky——踩上去時會發出一種叫 squeak 的尖細聲音。

lines.en: Charles played recordings of this sand, ocean waves and other relaxing sounds through speakers hidden in the park.
lines.zh: Charles 透過藏在公園裡的喇叭，播放這種沙子、海浪和其他讓人放鬆的聲音錄音。

lines.en: He created an art installation – a work of art designed to give people an interactive experience.
lines.zh: 他創作了一件 art installation（裝置藝術）——一種設計來讓人有互動體驗的藝術作品。

lines.en: By adding more relaxing sounds, Charles' installation actually made the park feel quieter.
lines.zh: 透過加入更多讓人放鬆的聲音，Charles 的裝置其實讓公園感覺更安靜了。

lines.en: It's an example of something that's counterintuitive, meaning it happens differently from how you would expect.
lines.zh: 這是 counterintuitive（違反直覺）的例子，意思是事情發生的方式和你預期的不同。

lines.en: What a great idea!
lines.zh: 真是個好點子！

lines.en: And similar soundscapes are now helping city dwellers relax in other cities too, including Tokyo and Barcelona.
lines.zh: 類似的聲景現在也在其他城市幫助居民放鬆，包括東京和巴塞隆納。

lines.en: Now Neil, you asked me a question about a very quiet sound – a whisper.
lines.zh: 好了，Neil，你問了我一個關於很安靜的聲音——悄悄話——的問題。

lines.en: So, are you going to reveal the correct answer?
lines.zh: 那你要揭曉正確答案了嗎？

lines.en: I asked you how loud a whisper is.
lines.zh: 我問你悄悄話有多大聲。

lines.en: Yes, and I said 13 decibels.
lines.zh: 對，我說 13 分貝。

lines.en: Well, 13 is an unlucky number and you are wrong.
lines.zh: 嗯，13 是個不吉利的數字，你答錯了。

lines.en: Ah!
lines.zh: 啊！

lines.en: It was actually 30.
lines.zh: 其實是 30 分貝。

lines.en: OK. Let's recap the vocabulary we've learned, starting with decibel – the unit for measuring sound.
lines.zh: 好。我們來複習學到的詞彙，首先是 decibel——計量聲音的單位。

lines.en: Someone who dresses loud likes to wear clothes with bright colours and bold designs.
lines.zh: 一個 dresses loud 的人，喜歡穿顏色鮮豔、設計大膽的衣服。

lines.en: If you can't handle something, you find it difficult to deal with.
lines.zh: 如果你 can't handle 某件事，就是你覺得很難應付它。

lines.en: An art installation is an artwork designed to create an interactive experience in a certain space.
lines.zh: art installation 是設計來在某個空間創造互動體驗的藝術作品。

lines.en: The adjective squeaky describes things which make a high-pitched sound like a mouse.
lines.zh: 形容詞 squeaky 形容會發出像老鼠那樣尖細聲音的東西。

lines.en: Squeak, squeak!
lines.zh: 吱吱、吱吱！

lines.en: And finally, if you call something counterintuitive, you mean it happens differently from how you would expect.
lines.zh: 最後，如果你說某件事 counterintuitive，意思是它發生的方式和你預期的不同。

lines.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but if you'd like to hear more about this and many other trending topics, you'll find more episodes and learning activities on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
lines.zh: 我們的六分鐘又到了，但如果你想聽更多這個主題和其他熱門話題，我們的網站 bbclearningenglish.com 上有更多集數和學習活動。

lines.en: See you again soon.
lines.zh: 很快再見。

lines.en: But for now, it's goodbye.
lines.zh: 但現在要說再見了。

lines.en: Goodbye...!
lines.zh: 再見……！
